chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl, from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

there are indeed seventy rows of the angels in the heaven. If all the people of the earth were to gather to count the number of each row among them, they would not count them; and they indeed profess religion through our wilayah.

key_terms.بِوَلَايَتِنَا: through our wilayah, meaning devotion and authority pertaining to the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.صَفًّا: a row or rank, here referring to ordered ranks of angels

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the angels and the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith affirms the immense number of the angels and presents their vast ranks as beyond human ability to enumerate. It also states that they are bound to the wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام, underscoring the cosmic and theological significance of that wilayah.
